subject: Hosted API: token cadence + burst window sanity check
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@cloudlocal.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cloudlocal.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 May 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: token cadence + burst window sanity check

Hi Sonia / Tom — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks so we can size pricing and concurrency correctly: 

1) Monthly token cadence: you mentioned the product team expects a steady-state monthly token footprint in the high single-digit millions with sporadic campaign-driven spikes. Can you confirm a baseline monthly figure (range is fine) and an expected peak month? For our working model I sketched three scenarios but need your confirmation:
   - conservative baseline: 3-6M tokens/month
   - expected baseline: 7-12M tokens/month
   - high/peak month: 15-25M tokens/month (campaigns)

2) Tokens per request: we need the round-trip token average (prompt + generation). If you don't have tokenized counts, a rough character or word average helps — we can convert.

3) Peak TPS and burst window: please confirm the expected requests/sec during your busiest minute and how long that burst typically lasts (e.g., 60–120s). We use that to size concurrency and offer realistic SLA guidance.

4) Target $/1M tokens (budget): you referenced a target range on the call — please confirm whether $700–$1,200 / 1M is still your expectation, or if procurement needs a firmer number for internal planning.

Next steps from our side once you confirm: we’ll populate the attached traffic estimate template, propose two pricing bands (committed monthly tiers + burst credit model), and include options for prefix caching/quantized model to hit lower unit costs.

Attachments: redwood-traffic-estimate-template.xlsx, pricing-summary-v2.pdf

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Sonia Patel <sonia@cloudlocal.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@cloudlocal.com>
Date: Thu, 15 May 2025 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: token cadence + burst window sanity check

Thanks Rafael — great recap. Quick answers below to help you draft the worksheet: 

- Monthly cadence: our current rollout schedule puts us at roughly 8–10M tokens/month for the next two quarters as we onboard more users. We have two marketing-driven months (June and November) where we expect heavy engagement and estimate 18–20M tokens in those months.

- Tokens per request: our typical interaction is a short system prompt + user input (avg ~120 tokens) and a medium-length assistant response (avg ~420 tokens). So round-trip avg ~= 540 tokens. There is variance by feature — some quick lookups are ~150 tokens round-trip, some long-form responses up to ~1,200 tokens.

- Peak TPS / burst window: for the upcoming launch we expect short bursts up to ~140 requests/sec at peak (roughly 75–90s windows during marketing pulses). Our backend does some client-side smoothing but these are the observed spikes in load tests.

- Budget $/1M: procurement is expecting to see options; they'd like to see a sweet spot around $900 / 1M as the target to evaluate value vs. other vendors. They are open to committed tiers if it reduces the effective unit price.

Happy to fill the attached baseline sheet — I’ll add conservative/expected/peak numbers by EOD Friday. CC’ing Tom for any additions.

Best,
Sonia
Sonia Patel
Head of Product, CloudLocal Inc
sonia@cloudlocal.com

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 16 May 2025 08:41:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hosted API: token cadence + burst window sanity check (internal)

Rafael — quick internal note after Sonia's numbers:

- With 540 tokens/req and spikes ~140 rps, peak token/sec ~= 75,600 tokens/sec. That maps to about ~4.5M tokens/minute during bursts — which is consistent with a 75–90s flash giving a single-burst bump of ~340M tokens (if the burst persisted). In practice Sonia's stated burst window (75–90s) implies we should size concurrency for ~140 rps and ensure autoscale ramp handles 60s warm-up.

- Pricing approach: propose 3-tier committed bands (6M, 12M, 24M monthly) + burst credits priced at a slightly higher uplift. Provide an example: 6M @ $1,050 / 1M; 12M @ $950 / 1M; 24M @ $850 / 1M. Add a short-term promo to hit Sonia's target of ~$900 effective for the first 6 months on a 12M commit.

- Ops advice: recommend prefix caching and short KV cache retention for common templates — should reduce avg token generation by ~10–15% for their chat paths. Also offer a quantized model variant for the non-critical flows (saves ~20–30% cost).

I can draft the pricing table if you want; also suggest we pre-populate the traffic template with the 3 scenarios Sonia offered.

— Priyom
Staff Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwoodinference.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sonia Patel <sonia@cloudlocal.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@cloudlocal.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 19 May 2025 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API: token cadence + burst window sanity check

Hi Sonia / Tom — thanks for the fast turnaround and the numbers — that’s very helpful. Confirming next steps and a proposed timeline: 

1) I will fill the attached redwood-traffic-estimate-template.xlsx with the three scenarios (conservative / expected / peak) using your 540 tokens/req baseline and the monthly ranges you gave. Expect that back to you by EOD Tuesday.

2) Pricing proposal (high level) — draft to review once you confirm the traffic sheet: 
   - Band A: 6M committed — $1,050 / 1M tokens
   - Band B: 12M committed — $950 / 1M tokens (we’ll include a 6-month promo to bring effective to ~$900 / 1M if you commit to 12M)
   - Band C: 24M committed — $850 / 1M tokens
   - Burst model: excess tokens billed at a 20% uplift over committed band rate; burst credits can be purchased monthly to smooth during campaigns.

3) Concurrency & SLOs: based on 140 rps and 540 tokens/req, we recommend an initial concurrency headroom for 160 rps with autoscale configured for a 60s ramp — Priyom will sketch the implementation notes to minimize cold starts.

4) Operational offers: we’ll include a short appendix with caching & quantization recommendations and an optional runbook for the campaign day.

5) Can you attach the baseline traffic numbers into the sheet and share any existing logs (sample 1–2 days of request counts) via the Drive link in the thread? That will let us tighten the proposal.

If this all looks good I’ll push a formal PDF proposal + simple SOW next week.

Best — Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwoodinference.com
